---
title: "Methods"
subtitle: "TCGA pan-cancer analytical framework"
---

## Analysis design

The TCGA exploration uses a standardized pan-cancer framework to
evaluate candidate kinase expression across the 33 TCGA cancer
projects.

Analyses are performed only where the required molecular and clinical
data are available.

## Expression data

Harmonized TCGA STAR gene-count files were used.

Expression analyses use the `tpm_unstranded` field.

For JAK3, expression was extracted across all available TCGA projects
and linked with sample-level and clinical metadata.

## Patient-level handling

Where more than one expression aliquot represented the same patient
and sample type, expression was collapsed to patient level using the
standardized pan-cancer workflow.

## Tumor versus normal

Primary malignant samples were compared with Solid Tissue Normal
samples where both groups were available.

The canonical tumor-normal analysis used the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied across
the tested cancer types.

## Matched tumor-normal

Where a patient had both tumor and normal samples, a paired
tumor-normal analysis was performed.

The paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used.

## Early-stage tumor versus normal

Early-stage tumors were defined using AJCC Stage I classifications,
including Stage IA, IB and IC where applicable.

Stage-I tumors were compared with Solid Tissue Normal samples.

## Stage-wise analysis

Stage analyses were performed only where sufficiently populated stage
groups were available.

Two complementary tests were retained:

- categorical differences across stage groups
- monotonic stage-expression trends

Kruskal-Wallis testing was used for categorical stage differences.

Spearman correlation was used to evaluate monotonic stage trends.

## Grade-wise analysis

Grade analyses were performed only where grade labels could be
standardized into interpretable ordered groups with sufficient sample
sizes.

Categorical grade differences and monotonic grade-expression trends
were both assessed.

## High or aberrant expression

Where normal tissue was available, the 95th percentile of the
normal-tissue TPM distribution was used as the reference threshold.

Tumors above this threshold were counted as showing high or aberrant
expression relative to the corresponding normal-tissue distribution.

## Survival analysis

Survival was treated as secondary evidence.

Curated TCGA Clinical Data Resource endpoints were used.

Continuous log2(TPM + 1) expression was evaluated using Cox
proportional-hazards models.

The following information was retained:

- sample size
- number of events
- hazard ratio
- 95% confidence interval
- false-discovery-rate-adjusted significance
- proportional-hazards diagnostic
- low-event-count flag

## Immune and inflammatory infiltration controls

TCGA RNA-seq represents bulk tissue, so observed expression may reflect
both malignant-cell biology and differences in immune or stromal cell
content.

Several complementary controls were therefore used.

### Leukocyte fraction

PanImmune leukocyte-fraction estimates were matched to TCGA tumors.

JAK3 expression was evaluated against leukocyte fraction using
correlation and regression analyses.

Stage and grade analyses were also repeated with measured leukocyte
fraction included as a covariate where possible.

### CIBERSORT

CIBERSORT relative immune-cell fractions were evaluated for 22 immune
cell types.

The analysis included:

- primary quality-filtered correlations
- all-sample sensitivity analysis
- leukocyte-fraction-adjusted cell-composition models
- robustness checks across these analytical layers

Because CIBERSORT relative fractions are compositional, cell types were
not entered simultaneously into one 22-variable regression model.

### Immune marker correlations

Expression-based immune controls used the following markers:

`PTPRC, CD3D, CD3E, MS4A1, CD79A, NKG7, LST1, TYROBP, FCER1G, CD68`

Marker expression was transformed using log2(TPM + 1).

### Multi-marker immune score

Within each cancer cohort, the ten log-transformed immune markers were
standardized separately.

The immune score was calculated as the equal-weighted mean of the
standardized marker values.

JAK3 itself was not included in this score.

### Immune-adjusted tumor-normal models

Three prespecified linear models were evaluated for both:

- all primary tumors versus normal tissue
- Stage-I tumors versus normal tissue

The models were:

1. unadjusted group association
2. group association adjusted for PTPRC/CD45
3. group association adjusted for the multi-marker immune score

Persistence after immune adjustment was evaluated within this same
linear-model family.

## Multiple testing

Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was used for
prespecified analysis families.

Both analysis-specific and broader pan-cancer adjusted results were
retained where appropriate.

## Sample sizes and limitations

Each analysis retains the relevant sample sizes and low-sample-size
flags.

Not every analytical module can be performed for every TCGA cancer
project because availability varies for:

- normal tissue
- matched tumor-normal samples
- Stage-I tumors
- stage annotation
- grade annotation
- survival events
- immune-infiltration estimates

## Interpretation

This analysis is an observational bulk-RNA pan-cancer screen.

A significant immune-adjusted association means that the expression
association remains after adjustment for the measured immune proxy.

It does not prove that expression originates from malignant cells.

Similarly, expression elevation in Stage-I tumors is compatible with
an early-disease association but does not establish a causal role in
tumor initiation.

## Reproducibility

Canonical final result tables and the final analysis pipeline are
retained in the repository.

Raw TCGA STAR files are not stored in version control.


## Multikinase extension

The completed JAK3 framework was extended to the candidate panel:

`JAK3, MET, HCK, LYN, DDR1, IRAK2, FJX1, EPHB1, RPS6KA2, EPHB2`

JAK3 was retained as the completed reference benchmark.

The same patient-level RNA, tumor-normal, early-stage, progression,
survival and immune-adjusted framework was applied across the panel.

## TCGA ATAC regulatory analysis

Official peak-to-gene regulatory links were obtained from the TCGA
pan-cancer ATAC Data S7 dataset.

Across the candidate panel, 51 official linked regulatory elements were
identified.

Some linked elements represented a single fixed-width ATAC peak, whereas
broader enhancer units contained multiple constituent peaks.

For broader units, the official `Summits` field was parsed and each summit
was mapped to the normalized TCGA ATAC matrix peak containing that summit.

All 74 constituent summits mapped successfully, retaining all 51 official
regulatory elements.

For regulatory units containing multiple constituent peaks, accessibility
was summarized using the mean of the constituent log2-normalized ATAC
values.

Technical replicates belonging to the same tissue fragment were collapsed
before patient-level analysis.

## Patient-matched ATAC-RNA analysis

Primary malignant RNA expression was summarized at patient level by
averaging TPM across eligible aliquots followed by transformation as:

`log2(TPM + 1)`

ATAC accessibility and RNA expression were matched by gene, cancer type,
patient and linked regulatory element.

Spearman correlation was calculated separately for each
gene-cancer-regulatory-element combination.

Analyses were classified according to matched sample size:

- at least 10 patients: primary analysis
- 5-9 patients: exploratory low-sample-size analysis
- fewer than 5 patients: not tested

Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment was applied to primary analyses.

A gene-specific global FDR was calculated across eligible tests for each
gene, and a second multikinase-wide FDR was calculated across all eligible
primary tests.

Direction concordance with the official Data S7 regulatory correlation was
also retained.

## Final multi-omic integration

Six normalized evidence domains were integrated:

1. primary tumor RNA
2. early-stage RNA
3. stage/grade progression
4. survival
5. immune-adjusted progression
6. ATAC-RNA regulatory coupling

The final multi-omic evidence index is the mean support across these six
domains.

The ATAC component was normalized by eligible-test significance and
cancer-level coverage so that genes with larger numbers of linked regulatory
elements were not automatically favored.

The integrated index and JAK3 benchmark-domain counts are descriptive
prioritization tools. They are not probabilities, causal estimates or formal
statistical rankings.

The original innate-memory classification is retained separately from the
TCGA validation score.
